title: Cranberry Orange Steel-Cut Oatmeal
changes_from_base: Steel-cut oats are soaked overnight in just-boiled water, so in the morning they need only a few minutes on the hob instead of the long simmer; they finish in orange juice and milk with dried cranberries, dark brown sugar and a touch of cardamom, topped with toasted flaked almonds.
summary: Tart-sweet cranberries and bright orange juice cut through creamy oats warmed with cardamom, topped with crunchy almonds for textural contrast.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Boil 720 ml water in the large saucepan, remove from the heat, add 175 g steel-cut oats and ½ tsp salt, cover and leave out overnight.

steps.title: Toast nuts
steps.text: Toast 45 g flaked almonds in a small dry pan 2-3 min and set aside.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: The morning after, stir in 120 ml orange juice, 120 ml milk, 60 g dried cranberries, 38 g dark brown sugar and ⅛ tsp cardamom.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring up to the boil on medium-high, then lower to medium and cook 4-6 min, stirring from time to time, until the oats are tender with a little bite and thickened like warm pudding.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Off the heat, rest 5 min, then scatter about 2 tbsp toasted almonds over each bowl.

tips: Use freshly squeezed or recently opened orange juice for the best flavour.
Dried cranberries can be tart; taste and add a touch more sweetness if you prefer.
Toast almonds in advance and store in an airtight container for up to a week.
storage: Serve warm; keep any leftovers in the fridge for 2 days and reheat gently on the stove with a splash of milk or juice. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
